name_zh: 南林与上南林大吉岭茶
processing: Typical of Darjeeling: orthodox black tea, withered, rolled, oxidised and dried. Moonshine lots are also sold from the Upper division.
harvest_season: First flush in spring and second flush lots are both sold.
appearance_dry: Twisted Darjeeling leaf in mixed olive and brown, greener in first flush.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in first flush, amber in second flush.
taste_profile: Typical of Darjeeling first flush: floral and brisk, with more fruit and body in second flush lots.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western-style. Use cooler water, about 85 C, and a shorter steep for delicate first flush.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush, sometimes with the division on the label: Upper Namring First Flush, Moonshine First Flush 2025. Buy the latest harvest, and check whether the label says Upper at all.
description:
Namring is a garden in the Teesta Valley area of Darjeeling, listed with Upper Namring as a single entry, and Upper Namring is a name that appears on its own on first flush lots.

The making is the usual orthodox process, with occasional special lots such as Moonshine.

Expect a first flush that behaves like other good Darjeeling: floral, brisk, and easy to spoil with boiling water. Second flush lots should be rounder.

When buying, read the label closely: Namring and Upper Namring are not the same lot. Look for the year and flush as well.
history:
The estate drew attention in 2018, when the London-based East India Company brand, whose tea master had surveyed 87 Darjeeling estates, bought 90 kg of an Upper Namring first flush.

Little else about its past could be confirmed here.
